summary.text: 家 is written with 宀 above 豕. The roof element is clear, but accounts differ on the lower sign: it may depict a pig beneath a roof, or represent an abbreviated sound element. Early uses for dwelling and household are reported; their order is unclear. Today 家 commonly means house, home, or family.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. One account reads 宀 and the lower sign as a dwelling with livestock beneath it, proposing “pig enclosure” as an original sense that later extended to human dwelling. The traditional Shuowen analysis reads 宀 as the dwelling element and the lower sign as abbreviated 豭, a sound element. 家 and 豭 have matching readings in modern Mandarin and in the cited Middle and Old Chinese reconstructions, making that analysis plausible if 豭 is the relevant sign. These matches do not establish the earliest sign’s identity or pronunciation, or prove a pig-enclosure origin.

components.text: 宀 is the roof or dwelling element in the graph. It is present as a full component; no separate earlier form is proposed.

The visible lower form is 豕. Some analyses read it as a pig contributing to a dwelling scene; the traditional analysis treats it as abbreviated 豭 used for sound. These competing readings leave the earliest sign’s identity and role unsettled. A proposed earlier form 𢑓 and its alteration to 豕 have not been verified.

sound_limitation.text: The readings are compatible if 豭 is the relevant sign, but do not establish that the visible 豕 represents 豭 or identify the earliest lower sign. No reading for proposed sign 𢑓 is established here.

sound.text: 家 and 豭 share the modern Mandarin reading, supporting sound compatibility under the traditional analysis but not proving the lower sign’s identity.
The cited Middle Chinese entries give matching readings for 家 and 豭, supporting compatibility if 豭 is the relevant sign.
The cited Old Chinese reconstructions match for 家 and 豭, supporting compatibility if 豭 is the relevant sign.

history.text: The regular-script form places 豕 beneath 宀. Shuowen describes the lower part as abbreviated 豭 used for sound, but this account does not show that 豕 developed graphically from 豭.
A proposal that the earliest lower sign was 𢑓 and was later altered or misread as 豕 remains unverified; the graphic sequence is unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The lower element’s earliest identity and role remain disputed: some analyses see a pig in a dwelling scene, while the traditional account treats it as an abbreviated sound element. “Pig enclosure” is a proposed original meaning, not an established one.
Matching readings for 家 and 豭 do not prove that the earliest lower sign was named 豭. No ancient pronunciation for the proposed depicted animal or sign is established.

senses.period: Oracle-bone uses are reported; dates of individual examples are unresolved
senses.text: Human dwelling uses are reported in oracle-bone contexts. A pig-enclosure origin has been proposed, but is not established as the earliest meaning.

senses.gloss: ancestral temple, family, royal house or court, or counted household
senses.period: Oracle-bone and bronze uses are reported; sequence unresolved
senses.text: Reported uses include ancestral temple and family, royal house or court, and households counted as 家. Their order and relationships are unclear.
家 commonly means house or home, and also family. How these senses relate chronologically to the reported early uses is unresolved.

developments.text: Dwelling and household or institutional uses are both reported early, but the evidence does not establish their order or a development from one to the other.
The modern senses are established, but their chronology and transition from the reported early uses are unresolved.

limitations.text: Reports of early uses do not provide a dated sequence of examined inscriptions, so the chronology of the senses remains unresolved.
The pig-enclosure account proposes a link from an enclosure to human dwelling; the traditional sound analysis offers a different account. Neither establishes the full history of the word’s meanings.

overview.text: 家 combines 宀, a roof or dwelling element, with a lower sign whose identity is disputed. Some read it as a pig beneath a roof; the traditional account treats it as abbreviated 豭 for sound. Early dwelling and household uses are reported, but their order is unclear.

components.text: 宀 contributes the roof or dwelling idea.
The lower sign may depict a pig or, in the traditional analysis, stand for abbreviated 豭 as a sound element; its earliest identity is unsettled.

relationships.text: In the proposed construction, 宀 contributes the roof or dwelling category.
Some analyses interpret the lower sign as a pig contributing to a scene of livestock kept beneath a dwelling.

The traditional account treats the visible lower form as abbreviated 豭 used for sound. Matching readings make this plausible under that analysis, but do not settle the earliest sign’s identity or prove a graphic derivation.
